:::writing{id="58316" variant="email" subject="The part of advertising that happens before Ads Manager"}
I taught a training this morning that technically had nothing to do with running ads.

No targeting, keywords, or campaign settings.

Instead, we spent the workshop inside The VAULT helping our Google Ads and Meta Ads Accelerator members define their unique value propositions. We worked through questions like:

- Who are you particularly well suited to serve?
- What are those clients really trying to create through their wedding?
- What do you do especially well that actually matters to them?
- Which things you’ve been calling “differentiators” are meaningful reasons to choose you, and which could be said by 20 competitors?

These questions have a lot to do with whether a couple will read your ad, visit your landing page, and feel like your business is worth a conversation.

Because before we can communicate why someone should choose you, we need to understand what makes you a meaningful choice for them.

This is the part of advertising that doesn’t happen inside the ad platform.

And it’s work we do together inside the Accelerators. You don’t need to arrive with all of these answers figured out.

I think that’s an important distinction when you’re deciding what kind of support you need to run ads.

Buying a course can leave you with 47 videos and a blank Ads Manager staring back at you. Even when you understand the instructions, you’re still responsible for figuring out how they apply to your business.

Inside our Accelerators, we help you work through those decisions.

We clarify your messaging, build your initial campaigns with you, and help you understand the data so you can learn how to make informed decisions about what comes next.

You’re building an advertising system around your business, with someone beside you who knows what that system needs to look like.

This morning, that meant stepping away from campaign settings and getting clearer on why the right couple would choose you. That clarity gives us something meaningful to build the ads around.

If this sounds like the kind of support you’ve been looking for, reply and tell me where you are with ads right now. We can talk through whether an Accelerator would be a good fit.

Whitney
:::

request.system: You write marketing copy for Wedding Industry Ads (WIA), an advertising agency for wedding venues and wedding professionals, in the voice of its co-founder, Whitney Hodges. The request below is from Whitney. Produce the one finished piece she asked for. If she asks for feedback on her own draft, return your improved version of her draft: keep what works and change only what makes it better. Never invent results, numbers, quotes, prices, dates or offer details that the request or the knowledge base does not state. Return only the finished copy, with no commentary.

We also decided that I **do NOT want to lead with "If you don't know your UVP, you shouldn't be running ads."** That could accidentally imply prospects need to figure out their UVP before joining us. The stronger message is that **they don't need to have this figured out already because this is part of the strategic work we do with them inside the Accelerators.**

The email should begin with:

**"I taught a training this morning that technically had nothing to do with running ads."**

The story is that instead of talking about targeting, keywords, or campaign settings, we spent the workshop defining their UVPs and working through questions like:

-  Who are you particularly well suited to serve? 
-  What are those clients really trying to create through their wedding? 
-  What do you do especially well that actually matters to them? 
-  Which things you've been calling "differentiators" are meaningful reasons to choose you, and which could be said by 20 competitors? 

One of the central lines we liked was:

**"This is the part of advertising that doesn't happen inside the ad platform."**

From there, the email should naturally transition into why our Accelerators are different from an online course. We're not simply teaching wedding pros where to click inside Ads Manager. We help them develop the strategy underneath the ads, clarify their messaging, build their initial campaigns, understand the data, and learn how to make decisions from it.

Another idea we liked:

**"You're building an advertising system around your business, with someone beside you who knows what that system needs to look like."**

We also liked the concept of contrasting the Accelerator experience with buying a course that leaves someone with **"47 videos and a blank Ads Manager staring back at you."**

**Voice/style:** Write in Whitney's founder voice for Wedding Industry Ads. Conversational, confident, insightful, specific, and genuinely human. Avoid generic AI marketing language, em dashes, "it's not X, it's Y" constructions, overly punchy one-line copy for the sake of punchiness, and cliché marketing language.

Keep in mind the content and sales frameworks we've been using from our marketing consultant Savannah Jordan: founder POV, behind-the-scenes/process content, demonstrating the depth of the methodology rather than simply claiming expertise, and using the content to create demand for the offer.

**Please start by putting the current email draft into an editable Writing Block. Do not substantially rewrite it yet. I want to edit it with you from there.**
